steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Social policy: government actions addressing social problems (education, welfare, crime, health). Sociology influences policy through evidence, evaluation and advocacy. | Key Fact: Evidence-based policy: using research evidence to design policies. Example: Sure Start was based on research showing early intervention improves outcomes. However, policies are also influenced by political ideology, economics and public opinion. | Key Fact: Positivist view: sociology should provide objective evidence for rational policymaking. Interpretivist view: sociology should give voice to lived experience to shape humane policy.
